root_cause: marmot-ts KeyPackageManager.create stores a KeyPackage locally before publishing and records it as published whatever the relays answered (NdkNetworkAdapter.publish never throws). A first publish no relay accepted therefore left the local count > 0, the app never published again, and peers' invites failed with 'has no key package'.
fix: After the startup stale-KeyPackage cleanup, the background KeyPackage task fetches our own kind 443/30443 events from the effective relays and counts only those a local KeyPackage backs (countBackedKeyPackageEvents). When a complete (not timed-out) fetch finds none, ensureKeyPackagesOnRelays publishes one last-resort KeyPackage again (the device's KeyPackages share one addressable slot, so one suffices), unless the init was cancelled. A timed-out or failed fetch never republishes.

tests_added.kinds: ensureKeyPackagesOnRelays decision cases (present / complete-empty republishes / timed-out / timed-out-with-hits / fetch throws / publish throws or publishes 0 => failed); countBackedKeyPackageEvents behavioural cases; publishKeyPackages count 1 is last-resort; source scan of the wiring (once, in the background task, after the cleanup, effective relays, no limit, cancelled guard). Gap (accepted, no-jsdom convention): no e2e for a rejected first publish (the relay would have to reject the app's own publish).

mutation.survivors: 1 NoCoverage, pre-existing: replenishKeyPackagesIfNeeded's DEFAULT_RELAYS default parameter (every caller passes relays).

e2e.result: non-relay 72 passed; relay 350 passed, 1 failed, 2 did not run, 19 skipped; no INVALID marker. The failure is dm-block-cross-tab.spec.ts:84, the known renderer click stall (30 s in performing click action on chat-send-btn; backlog dm-composer-enter-press-hangs-30s, sighting recorded). It also stalls without this fix (1 of 13 isolated baseline runs, item-12 source stashed); with the fix 3 of 8 isolated runs stalled — not significant at these sizes, recorded on the finding.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The first wiring sat beside, not after, an existing background cleanup that deletes relay KeyPackages no local one backs; only codex traced that interaction. The startup KeyPackage logic is spread over three create sites (init count===0, background readiness, and now the repair).
retrospective.surprised_by: network.request hides fetch timeouts as an empty result, so it cannot distinguish 'relays hold none' from 'relays did not answer'; the repair needed fetchEventsWithTimeout directly.
